name: Brussels sprouts
why_now: Brussels sprouts are a cool-season crop, and they arrive in November sweeter than they'll be at any other time; a little cold makes them convert starch to sugar. Crisped hard, their outer leaves go brown and nutty and the centers turn tender.
how_to_choose: Small, tight, bright green heads, an inch or so across
No yellow outer leaves or black spots
Similar sizes, so they cook evenly
buy_this_much: 1 lb for the salmon and lentils.
price_note: Sold loose by the pound or in bags. Loose lets you pick small, even ones.

flavor_paths.name: Air fryer
flavor_paths.description: Halved, 350°F, tossed halfway, until crisp at the edges.

flavor_paths.name: With lentils
flavor_paths.description: Folded into lentils dressed with the jar's brine.

flavor_paths.name: With fish sauce
flavor_paths.description: Tossed hot with a spoonful of fish sauce and chile.

weekday_uses: Crisped in the air fryer and folded into warm lentils under salmon
Leftovers tossed with fish sauce and chile, beside rice
weekend_use: Halved and crisped, under two fried eggs.
storage: In the fridge, unwashed, in a bag, for up to a week. Trim them just before cooking.
one_thing_to_learn: Overcooked Brussels sprouts smell like cabbage because they are cabbage. Cooked hot and fast, cut side down or in moving hot air, they brown before the sulfur builds up.
